“The 2020s are on course to have the lowest growth in incomes of any decade on record,” Resolution’s post-budget report said, “because of rising taxes and import prices.”

Taxing the rich is no longer an easy option, with Bloomberg analysis last month showing that the share of total income tax paid by the highest earners in the UK has doubled in less than two decades — a hit of £100 billion. That comes on top of other raids targeting the wealthy on everything from private school fees and expensive houses to Britain’s long-standing non-domiciled regime.

Work by the Institute for Fiscal Studies in 2024 showed that the share of tax paid by the top 1% of income taxpayers rose from 25% in 2010-2011 to 28.5% in 2023-2024, while income and payroll taxes took a smaller fraction of the earnings of a single full-time median earner with no children than at any time for almost 50 years.

title: BYD earnings dampen hopes Chinese car stocks will reverse rout
article:
(Oct 30): BYD Co’s latest earnings signal that this year’s surge in car exports won’t be enough to recapture lost momentum in Chinese auto stocks.

Its shares slipped as much as 2.4% in Hong Kong on Friday after the country’s biggest carmaker reported third-quarter profits and revenue that missed analysts’ estimates, overshadowing overseas sales more than doubling from a year ago. An export-led growth story didn’t help BYD’s nearest local competitor, Geely Automobile Holdings Ltd, either as its stock fell for a second day.

The two auto giants’ failure to reinvigorate enthusiasm bodes ill for a once high-flying industry that investors have soured on for more than a year. China’s car market, the world’s largest, continues to shrink and more recently some authorities abroad have stepped up efforts to slow down the flood of Chinese imports.

“Exports face new headwinds just as they have become a key profit driver for BYD,” said Joanna Chen, an analyst at Bloomberg Intelligence. Investors will focus on how fast BYD can ramp up overseas production, and how profitably it can make cars overseas compared with back in China, she said.

Some companies, particularly foreign brands, have been even worse off. Volkswagen AG, Europe’s largest carmaker, on Thursday reported a loss for the latest quarter, largely because of exposure to China.

See also: China builds its GDP on competitive advantage

In the run-up to the earnings reports, signs emerged that some investors were turning more bullish on BYD as short sellers pared back bets against the stock, which has fallen nearly 30% in Hong Kong this year, heading for its biggest annual drop since 2011.

Profit climbed 28% from a year earlier but fell short of the average analyst estimate compiled by Bloomberg by 17%. Revenue was about 8% less than what analysts had estimated.

Scale gains were absorbed by cost pressures, according to a research note from analysts at Jefferies, who have a 'hold' rating on BYD shares.

See also: Geely's profit climbs as rising exports offset China slump

The results also pointed to a build-up of inventory, currency-related losses amid the continued appreciation of the Chinese yuan and a big drop in income from financial investments, the Shenzhen-based carmaker disclosed.

BYD and other Chinese carmakers are facing slowing demand and intense price competition domestically, making a pivot overseas — where their budget-friendly, technology-focused models make more money — critical to survival.

But their popularity is creating new hurdles, particularly in Europe, where Chinese automakers outsold Japanese rivals for the first time ever for a full quarter. Registrations of Chinese-branded cars roughly doubled to make up 12.7% of total sales across the region, led by hybrids, according to market researcher Dataforce. Five years ago, Chinese brands accounted for barely 1% of European sales.

The European Union has already imposed extra tariffs on China-made battery-electric vehicles, and this month agreed in principle to curb fast-growing imports of hybrid cars from China. Plug-in hybrid vehicles have accounted for nearly half of BYD’s passenger car sales.

The restrictions are spurring BYD to spend billions of dollars to build a physical presence in Europe. Its first factory in the region, located in Hungary, is set to start mass production in the fourth quarter, Stella Li, the executive vice-president who heads the company’s overseas business, said this month. France and Spain are on the shortlist for future plants, and the carmaker wants to build a European workforce of about 40,000 employees by the end of the decade, she said.

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

For the first nine months of the year, deliveries have lagged behind sales during the same period a year earlier, putting its annual sales target — five million to 5.5 million — further out of reach.

However, the company did see a recovery in deliveries at home as it ramped up production of its latest generation of Blade batteries, with August and September local shipments marking month-over-month increases.

The company is betting on the fast-charging system to further boost sales, and has brought the first sport utility vehicle equipped with the latest batteries to Europe during the Paris Motor Show. Li also confirmed earlier this month that BYD had ordered 10 more vessels, in addition to its operational fleet of eight cargo ships.

Yet domestic pressure is set to continue into next year. China’s total sales are set to tumble 22% this year to just 18.5 million vehicles, the Passenger Car Association estimates. The group expects average growth of 2% next year, a pace that it describes as a weak recovery rather than a strong rebound.

title: Nvidia CEO says ties to Singapore company in spy probe were ‘normal’
article:
(Oct 30): Nvidia Corp chief executive officer Jensen Huang said the chipmaker’s dealings with Megaspeed International were “normal and not unusual” following a New York Times report that one of the Singapore firm’s executives is under investigation for spying on behalf of China.

Nvidia’s relationship with Megaspeed’s officials was proper, and the chipmaker has checked to ensure that Megaspeed didn’t illegally send its artificial intelligence (AI) processors to China, Huang said in an interview Thursday. That country is barred from buying Nvidia’s powerful AI chips — known as graphics processing units, or GPUs — under US export rules.

“We’ve studied all their deployments of our GPUs and counted every one,” he said in the interview. “And I think the US government also has as well.”

The remarks follow a Times story that the US government is investigating an executive from Megaspeed for allegedly providing information to the Chinese government. Huang Le has previously been pictured with Nvidia’s leader on social media, and the story reports that she may have been serving as a Chinese agent aiming to evade chip export controls.

Asked about the report at a regular daily briefing in Beijing, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said it was “unsubstantiated and purely a smear against China”.

In the interview, Huang said that his interactions with her were typical of those with Chinese customers and executives. She’s no longer with Megaspeed, he said.

See also: Neocloud troubles won’t end the AI boom

“Our relationship, our interactions, have been related to Megaspeed, and it was all completely normal and not unusual,” Huang said. The CEO said he hadn’t been informed by the US government of its suspicions about Huang Le.

The growing geopolitical rivalry between the US and China has led to increasing clampdowns by Washington on exports of key American technology. That’s cut off Nvidia from a lucrative source of revenue in China, the largest market for chips.

The company has received some latitude to ship a limited amount of older AI-related products to the Asian country under the Trump administration. That approval hasn’t resulted in a material amount of shipments, at least in part because Beijing has sought to limit the deliveries itself in an effort to foster its own chip industry.

See also: INSEAD gets US$3 mil from Google.org and DeepMind to study AI’s effect on work

Nonetheless, the restrictions on exports have led to investigations and charges of smuggling of Nvidia’s best products to China — something the company has said is an insignificant issue. Megaspeed is one of a group of companies that Bloomberg News and others have reported may have tried to illegally divert shipments of chips intended for data centres outside of China into that country.

title: Record Binance hack shows no crypto firm is too big to breach
article:
(Oct 30): A security breach at Binance involving up to US$6.3 billion ($8.1 billion) is the biggest crypto hack on record, raising fresh questions about the industry’s ability to protect digital assets as it seeks to woo traditional finance.

The incident at the world’s largest crypto exchange highlights how vulnerabilities can extend even to the biggest players.

“This is the largest cyber theft on record, not just the largest in crypto,” said Aneirin Flynn, chief executive officer of cybersecurity technology firm FailSafe. “This will damage confidence in crypto. The industry is courting institutional capital, but institutions will not overlook repeated failures in custody and security.”

So far the total impact sits at around US$6.3 billion, Binance said in a post on X on Friday, adding that it will make good all losses. Binance has temporarily suspended withdrawals on the exchange.

The hack extends a string of costly breaches across the cryptocurrency industry. In February 2025, Dubai-based Bybit suffered a US$1.5 billion theft, then the largest single crypto heist on record. The FBI blamed North Korean hackers, who dispersed the stolen assets across thousands of addresses on multiple blockchains.

See also: Binance says US$6.3 bil impacted as crypto reels from hack

There have been several big heists in recent months.

In August, hackers absconded with more than US$100 million worth of bitcoin from thousands of wallets secured by hardware devices made by Canada-based Coinkite Inc. The attack exploited a software flaw that made the private keys protecting the crypto predictable.

In September, crypto exchange Bitget said attackers made off with about US$388 million. And in October, criminals tampered with Ledger hardware wallets distributed through a Southeast Asian reseller, with blockchain researchers estimating losses of more than US$90 million. Ledger said its own systems weren’t breached.

See also: Bitcoin dips below US$80,000 as AI-related market selloff deepens

Prediction market Polymarket temporarily halted trading this week after a third-party provider was compromised, with more than US$2.5 million lost.

The incidents highlight the breadth of vulnerabilities facing crypto businesses, from their own wallets and technology systems to supply chains and outside providers.

The risks extend beyond crypto-native companies. In South Korea, a series of cyberattacks has hit financial institutions in recent weeks, including cryptocurrency exchange Bithumb Co, Mirae Asset Global Investments Co and Daishin Securities Co reporting unauthorised access that exposed user data.

The breaches have raised questions about the security of outsourced systems and third-party technology providers as financial firms increasingly rely on interconnected digital infrastructure.

“Every bank, asset manager and exchange operator trying to put treasuries, funds or equities on-chain has to pick a settlement layer, and until tonight ‘the biggest exchange’ was a defensible answer,” said Luca Parlamento, founder and chief investment officer at D2 Finance. “Now it’s an unsecured credit decision.” D2 Finance doesn’t have any transactions on Binance, Parlamento said.

Initial investigation suggests that the security incident may involve an engineer’s compromised laptop, Binance said in its post.

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

According to blockchain analytics firm TRM Labs, North Korea is behind the hack. It said preparation started at least 36 hours before the theft.

“On the evening of October 29, billions of dollars in crypto began leaving wallets belonging to Binance” across 10 blockchains — including bitcoin, ethereum, solana and XRP — and flowing to addresses controlled by a single attacker, TRM said.

For exchanges holding billions of dollars in customer assets, the challenge is no longer simply securing private keys or keeping most funds in offline storage. Wallet systems increasingly involve multiple signers, automated transaction processes, smart-contract permissions and external service providers.

“The lesson for an allocator isn’t that crypto is risky. It’s that an exchange balance is an unsecured loan to a company that can lose its keys,” Parlamento said.

title: When Intel sneezes, AEM catches a cold
article:
The best thing about Mainboard-listed AEM Holdings (SGX:AWX ) is also the worst thing about it. The local chip-testing company has been riding high on the global AI boom. That has allowed AEM’s stock price to go up by more than seven-fold over the past year, hitting a peak of $11.58.

But tying one’s fortunes to a single factor makes it a single point of risk. These days, investors are beginning to question the value of all the capital tech companies have been pouring into AI. Google’s parent company, Alphabet endured a blood bath on Oct 29, losing US$500 billion in market value, after reporting its second consecutive quarter of negative free cash flow.

The past few weeks have been a period of reckoning for AEM as well. AEM’s stock price has been trending downwards since Oct 9 when it was originally sitting at $11.18. The worst, however, had yet to come. AEM opened at $7.34 on Oct 30, nearly 10% lower than its closing price a day before. AEM’s shares were trading at $7.35 as at 3 pm.

That drubbing was not due to any disclosures from AEM itself. Afterall, the company had announced its earnings for 1HFY2026 less than three months ago on Aug 12. At the time, AEM had reported a whopping 876% y-o-y increase in its earnings to $30.8 million. Instead, the key driver behind AEM’s stock price plummet on Oct 30 might have been the underwhelming earnings announcement from one of its customers, Intel.

On Oct 29, Intel reported its earnings for 3QFY2026. The chip giant’s revenue for the third quarter was up 20% y-o-y at US$16.5 billion. While Intel says its revenue figure is US$0.2 billion above its outlook in July, it is still lower than the US$16.6 billion analysts were forecasting. What was even more troubling were the remarks made by Intel’s CEO Lip-Bu Tan on the poor outlook for central processing unit (CPU) sales.

“In recent weeks, our customers began signalling a PC slowdown based on memory prices and availability,” Tan told analysts during the company’s earnings call. “Year-to-date system end-point prices have increased significantly placing additional pressure on already limited IT budgets.”

See also: South Korea's FuriosaAI quadruples value to US$2.9 bil in Nvidia chase

According to Tan, the correction that has been taking place within the personal computer (PC) market has accelerated over the last two months. Intel’s original equipment manufacturer (OEM) partners have tried to match the softer sell thru by managing their inventory aggressively, Tan adds. He expects current market conditions to persist until memory availability and prices begin to normalise.

“I am disappointed that we were not able to meet strong customer demand in this quarter. We face near term challenges, including manufacturing supply shortages, the unprecedented memory crunch, and the resulting softness in PC demand,” Tan says.

Intel is a major customer of AEM. That means Intel’s bad news could very well be AEM’s bad news. To be clear, AEM does not reveal the amount of revenue it draws from Intel. In its annual report for FY2026, AEM said one customer from its test cell solutions segment was responsible for over $152 million out of the group’s total revenue of $399 million but it did not specify who that company was. That said, most analysts view Intel as a larger driver of AEM’s revenue. DBS Group Research analyst Amanda Tan said in a July 24 report on AEM that Intel accounts for about 25% of her FY2026 revenue forecast.

See also: Nvidia-backed firm launches US$3.1 bil GPU loan in market

Incidentally, Tan was still bullish on CPUs earlier this month. The Intel chief was speaking on a panel at DBS’s Asia Future Forward Conference on Oct 12 when he told attendees that CPUs were actually more useful than GPUs (graphic processing units) when it comes to certain aspects of AI training.

“We are excited [that] the CPU demand is so strong,” Tan says. “The CPU, actually, is more useful when you do the inference orchestrations and reinforcement learning. A lot of frontier model [companies], they have been asking, ‘Lip-Bu, we need more CPU.’ So, I think overall that is a positive for us.”

title: SNB reports nine-month profit on foreign currencies and gold
article:
(Oct 30): The Swiss National Bank reported a solid nine-month profit thanks to its foreign-currency portfolio and gold holdings.

The SNB earned 44.2 billion francs (US$5.4 billion) from January through September, it said in a statement on Friday. That raised the likelihood of a year-end payout to the Swiss government.

The central bank’s hoard of assets in foreign currencies — including its large equities portfolio — delivered a profit of 43.3 billion francs. The value of the gold held by the central bank increased by 1.2 billion francs.

Positions in Swiss francs generated a gain of 0.1 billion francs. Those earnings include negative interest charged on oversized commercial-bank reserves held at the SNB. Sight deposits exceeding a certain threshold are subject to this since the central bank cut its benchmark rate to zero last year.

The SNB’s results don’t influence monetary policy and are heavily influenced by asset price changes, with quarterly numbers often having little bearing on final result for the year.

They are however fiscally important for the federal government and Switzerland’s cantons, or states. In cases of annual losses, the central bank at times can’t make a payout, which is particularly painful for smaller Swiss regions.

See also: ECB’s Moulin sees policy as measured with most prices stable

title: ECB’s Moulin sees policy as measured with most prices stable
article:
(Oct 30): The European Central Bank (ECB) is responding in a measured way to inflation as most prices are stable and pressures are largely imported rather than driven by domestic factors, Governing Council member Emmanuel Moulin said.

At its meeting on Thursday, the central bank refrained from a third increase in borrowing costs since the Iran war pushed up energy prices. But officials discussed the possibility of a hike and president Christine Lagarde said the direction of travel for future policy is “clear.”

“Excluding energy and fresh produce, prices remain relatively stable. Similarly, we aren’t seeing spillover effects to salaries at this stage,” Moulin said in an interview with French newspaper La Montagne. “In the current situation, with inflation mainly imported, the ECB is adopting a measured approach.”

Moulin, who’s also governor of the Bank of France, said the ECB will continue to follow the inflation situation “very closely” and take action at future meetings depending on data it has.

He reiterated his opposition to French far-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon’s proposal to cancel or freeze sovereign debt held by the Bank of France. Moulin said doing so would create a balance-sheet hole and spark difficulties for the entire euro area, without any gain for public finances.

“France has never defaulted on its debt since 1797,” he said. “Talking about such a cancellation would not only achieve very little, but it is already costing us as it creates distrust toward our country.”

See also: Jio Platforms adds US$36 bil in value after India IPO surge

Moulin also said it’s not the ECB’s job to step into help France with its fiscal challenges, which have spooked investors in recent weeks, sparking a selloff of bonds and driving up borrowing costs.

“Our fiscal problems should be dealt with in France, notably by voting a budget that reduces the deficit,” he said. “That’s what will enable us to reassure investors on the direction the country is going.”

title: Indian AI firm seeks US$3 bil financing for Nvidia chips order — Bloomberg
article:
(Oct 30): Indian AI infrastructure firm AM Intelligence is seeking to raise as much as US$3 billion to fund a previously announced purchase of Nvidia Corp’s next-generation chips, according to people familiar with the matter, the latest sign that the technology’s boom is driving a debt binge.

The funding package for the company, established by the founders of renewable energy producer Greenko Group Plc, could comprise of bonds and bank loans, among others, said the people who asked not to be identified discussing private details.

The breakdown between the various options is still being finalised and the firm also expects to get US$300 million in advance payment from potential offtakers, the people said. Talks are still in the initial stages and terms could change.

A representative for AM Intelligence declined to comment. Nvidia didn’t respond to requests for comment.

The planned deal shows how the race to fund the AI infrastructure buildout in Asia and elsewhere is giving rise to increasingly layered financing structures, combining traditional bank lending with private capital and upfront commitments from customers as developers seek billions of dollars to secure the latest generation of processors.

Globally, the borrowing binge tied to the AI boom has flooded markets with more than US$650 billion of debt in less than two years, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.

See also: Google shares drop after 3Q sales miss reignites fears over AI

AM Intelligence said in August that it had ordered Vera Rubin chips under an US$8 billion project, as it seeks to become one of the first adopters of the advanced computing platform in Asia. The project is part of a broader plan to set up one-gigawatt of computing capacity. Its Hyderabad facility aims to run trillion-parameter AI models and next-generation agentic AI applications.An estimated US$90 billion in investment opportunity could emerge across India’s data centre value chain by fiscal year 2035, extending beyond capacity additions into related infrastructure and services, according to a KPMG report released in July.

title: Keppel REIT’s response on the acquisition of Keppel South Central
article:
I refer to your article “Keppel REIT’s latest acquisition yet another unfavourable deal for minorities”, published on Oct 26, 2026 and would like to set out why Keppel REIT Management believes the acquisition of Keppel South Central is in the interests of Keppel REIT and all its Unitholders.

In considering the acquisition, we have focused on both its near-term income contribution and its potential to create value for Unitholders over the longer term.

Leasing at Keppel South Central has been progressing well with committed leases and leases in the process of documentation increasing from 52.7% as of Sept 30, 2026 to approximately 60% as of mid-October 2026. A further 20% of space is also under negotiation1, providing good visibility on continued lease-up. This is supported by positive Singapore office market fundamentals, with Grade-A CBD office vacancy expected to drop to 3.8%2 by 2030 and rents continuing to grow amid limited new supply.

While leasing in terms of achieved rental rate is above the acquisition assumptions and continues to progress, the proposed arrangement3 with Keppel REIT’s sponsor, Keppel, provides Unitholders with income stability for a period of up to five years after completion of the transaction. Unlike conventional income support arrangements, it is backed by current rents at Keppel South Central, with the average rent of approximately $11.30 psf already above the $11.15 psf rent assumed under the arrangement. At the same time, there remains upside from continued lease-up, with the potential for higher rents as leasing progresses from the low-to-mid floors to the mid-to-high floors.

The acquisition is DPU-accretive on a pro forma basis at 2.01%4, after taking into account adjustments to reflect the significant portfolio movements over the past year. Even without these adjustments, the acquisition would remain DPU accretive at 1.81% based on actual FY2025 DPU.

Keppel REIT has a long track record of acquiring quality assets, which have contributed recurring income and capital appreciation over time. This year, Keppel REIT’s focus was on active asset management and realising divestments, with a view to optimise the portfolio and strengthen its balance sheet to better position Keppel REIT in its core markets.

The divestments of KR Ginza II in Japan and T Tower in Seoul, announced last quarter, were at good premiums to their latest valuations and our historical entry prices. With divestments on track, we began focusing on how the portfolio can be optimised to enhance DPU for Unitholders over the long term. The unit buyback plan5 referred to in the announcement on the divestment of T Tower was part of the enhancement but that would have limited effect on replacing the DPU contribution from the divestments.

Thus, as part of Keppel REIT’s portfolio optimisation, we considered the Keppel South Central opportunity carefully, cognisant that it is still in pre-stabilisation stage. High-quality Singapore CBD assets are usually tightly held and typically trade at low cap rates. At an agreed property value of $626.2 million6, equivalent to approximately $2,350 psf, Keppel REIT is acquiring at an attractive initial property yield of 4.3%. We believe the terms agreed for Keppel South Central, including the certainty of income for up to five years, are attractive for Keppel REIT.

Keppel REIT remains focused on delivering stable distributions and sustainable long-term total returns to all Unitholders and believes Keppel South Central will contribute meaningfully to that for many years to come.

1Refer to Keppel Ltd’s media release dated Oct, 20, 2026 titled “Keppel to divest 51% stake in Keppel South Central for about $611 million to Keppel REIT” for further details.

3Based on Keppel REIT’s arrangement with the Vendor for the transaction. Refer to the announcement titled “Proposed acquisition of 51.0% interest in Keppel South Central” for further details.

4Assumes the proposed acquisition of Keppel South Central and the divestments of T Tower and KR Ginza II had been completed on Jan 1, 2025 and taking into account certain adjustments. Refer to the announcement titled “Proposed acquisition of 51.0% interest in Keppel South Central” for further details.

5Subject to prevailing market conditions and applicable laws and regulations. Refer to the announcement titled “Keppel REIT to crystallise value through divestment of T Tower in Seoul” dated Sept 23, 2026.

6The agreed property value of Keppel South Central takes into account independent valuations conducted by Colliers International Consultancy & Valuation (Singapore) and CBRE, which were commissioned by the trustee of Keppel REIT and the Manager respectively. Keppel South Central was valued at $646.7 million and $652.0 million by Colliers and CBRE respectively as of Sept 30, 2026, including the income support arrangement.

Chua Hsien Yang is CEO of Keppel REIT Management, the manager of Keppel REIT

title: Mapletree Investments prepares for IPO early next year
article:
During Mapletree Pan Asia Commercial Trust’s (MPACT) results briefing, what stood out was a question by Mervin Song, real assets and REITs analyst at JP Morgan, on the IPO of Mapletree Investments. “Ahead of the sponsors' potential listing next year, is it time for a more radical change in MPACT’s strategy? Would management of MPACT recommend to the board and sponsors to consider splitting MPACT into two REITs: Mapletree Singapore Trust and Mapletree Outside Singapore Trust to unlock value?”

Sharon Lim, CEO of MPACT’s manager, said: “Anything about the broader strategy of the group — that should be redirected to the group.”

So, the cat is out of the bag. It appears that the REIT and analyst community are aware that Mapletree Investments is at an advanced stage of the IPO process.

A well-known analyst has joined Mapletree in a strategy role for the IPO, market watchers say.

Market watchers have also identifed the CEO and chairman of the potential IPO. The listed entity will comprise entirely of a fund management structure and own 10% to 15% of the REITs, market watchers say.

Mapletree Investments is likely to be split into a ListCo and an AssetCo. The ListCo will comprise the fee-generating activities of the REITs, private funds, joint ventures and development properties.

See also: Anthropic IPO may spark AI rally as short bets on tech pile up

Meanwhile, the AssetCo will hold the balance sheet assets of the REITs, private funds, JVs and development properties.

The ListCo will manage the assets in AssetCo.

The group CEO of ListCo will be Goh Chye Boon. Lily Ler (formerly CEO of Mapletree Industrial Trust Management), Wong Mun Hong, Chua Tiow Chye and Hiew Yoon Khong will be in the steering committee.

See also: Mi Material closes at $1.82 on first day of trading; Stabilisation manager bought 1.5 mil shares at IPO price of $1.80

When asked, a Mapletree Investments spokesperson says: "As a matter of policy, we do not comment on market rumours. Any material information, should it arise, will be communicated through the appropriate channels."

Other market watchers suggest that the potential IPO of Mapletree Investments is part of a broader strategy by Singapore Inc to revive the stock market. Notably, there have been rumblings of big listings such as PSA, Singapore Power and even Changi Airport Group, although this appears unlikely in the near term.

Specifically on MPACT, Lim said the manager is planning a substantive asset enhancement initiative (AEI) on VivoCity. “Our back of the house which is our drop-off point, can be turned to some form of a front. So much traffic passes there, it's quite a shame that it's technically a back of a house. The back of this house connects to our hypermarket and H&M. I think there is a lot of work that we can do to change the space and add a new cluster. We are at a very advanced drafting stage. We don't see big hurdles, but we have not tendered out to get all the numbers but it will provide positive ROI. We are trying to minimise disruption. But we need disruption before we can get the numbers,” Lim elaborates.

In an initial update, JP Morgan points out that the key positives included Mapletree Business City's committed occupancy rising to 95.4% from 94.3% in 1QFY2027 ended June 30 and 93% a year ago, with committed leases beginning to contribute from 3QFY2027.

VivoCity remained strong, with 2QFY2027 NPI up 5% y-o-y, committed occupancy at 100%, 1HFY2027 rental reversion of +15.0% and 2QFY2027 tenant sales growth of 3.3% y-o-y.

Finance expenses fell 14.4% y-o-y in 1HFY2027, helping limit the decline in DPU to 3.0% despite NPI falling 6.5%.

The update points to China's year-to-date (1HFY2027) rental reversion of -29.9% as a key negative. Festival Walk's rental reversion during the first half was -15.6%. Japan's committed occupancy was only 57.5% (+1.5% ppt q-o-q), reflecting the previously disclosed Fujitsu Makuhari non-renewal.

"Festival Walk's occupancy improved to 99.9% and tenant sales rose 3.7% y-o-y in 2QFY2027, but negative reversions (-15.6% in 1HFY2027, from -9.1% in 1QFY2027) remain a drag on income.

MPACT’s weighted average cost of debt edged up to 2.95% from 2.94% in 1QFY2027, and management said the scope for further finance-cost savings has narrowed as rates rise. Aggregate leverage also increased to 38.1% from 37.7% in 1QFY2027," JP Morgan says.

title: US-owned startup plans US$600 mil Malaysia rare-earth refinery
article:
(Oct 30): A US majority-owned startup plans to invest US$600 million in a rare-earth refinery in Malaysia, seeking to develop a new source of the critical minerals as Washington pushes to reduce its reliance on China.

DTEC Mineral and Metal Technology expects to set up the plant in the Southeast Asian country within the next three years, chief executive Officer Milan Perlly said in an interview. It became the first company to receive permission recently under Malaysia’s eased export rules to ship unprocessed rare-earth material to the US.

The project would support efforts by Malaysia and the US to develop new sources of rare earths outside China, which dominates the processing of the minerals. Rare earths are essential for products ranging from electric vehicles and electronics to wind turbines and advanced weapons.

“The larger goal is to make Malaysia the rare-earth elements processing hub for ionic clay in the region,” Perlly said.

Much of Malaysia’s identified rare-earth resources are found in so-called ion-adsorption clay deposits, where the elements are loosely bound to clay rather than locked in hard rock, potentially making them easier and cheaper to extract. They can contain sought-after heavy rare earths used in high-performance magnets and other advanced technologies.

DTEC Mineral’s first refinery would have capacity to process 5,000 metric tons of rare-earth material annually, Perlly said. The company ultimately aims to build two facilities in Malaysia with combined capacity of 10,000 tons a year.

See also: Light at the end of the tunnel for KL’s 8 Conlay?

“The US wants us to build 10,000 metric tons output,” he said. “My goal is to put one plant on the east coast for 5,000 metric tons, a second plant on the west coast.”

DTEC Mineral is considering locations after holding talks with officials in the Malaysian states of Kedah, Terengganu, Perak and Negeri Sembilan, he said. The facilities would expand Malaysia’s role in the rare-earth industry beyond the processing operations of Australia’s Lynas Rare Earths Ltd., which runs a major plant in Pahang state.

DTEC Mineral intends to develop locally sourced ionic-clay deposits and eventually operate its own mine in Malaysia, Perlly said. Malaysia has identified an estimated 16.1 million tons of rare-earth resources, according to government estimates, much of which has yet to be proven commercially viable.

See also: Menara Tun Perak, Maybank’s former Kuala Lumpur headquarters, up for sale: sources

The company is preparing to ship about 30 tons of unprocessed rare-earth material to the US for research after receiving approval to export as much as 700 tons, he said. The shipment is intended to help determine the composition of the material and the most suitable processing technology, according to Perlly.

Perlly, a Malaysian-born US citizen who formerly worked at Capital One, and business partner David Greer own 51% of DTEC Mineral. Malaysian firm DTEC Engineering and Construction holds the remaining 49%.

DTEC Mineral has ambitions to list in Malaysia and on either the Nasdaq or New York Stock Exchange, Perlly said.

The firm was part of a trade and critical minerals pact signed between US President Donald Trump and Malaysian Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim last year. Under the agreement, DTEC is eligible for funding from Export–Import Bank of the United States, US International Development Finance Corporation and the Department of Defense, according to DTEC’s website.

title: Tuas Power signs MoU to import up to 500 MW of hydropower from Lao PDR
article:
Local power generator Tuas Power has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Électricité du Laos (EDL) and Phongsupthavy Group (PTSG) to explore an arrangement for EDL and PTSG to supply Singapore with up to 500 MW of hydropower from Lao PDR for a term of 5-15 years potentially.

Under the MoU, Tuas Power will import 100 MW in the first contract year, 300 MW in the second and 500MW from the third year onwards. The arrangement potentially provides Tuas Power with renewable hydropower that can be paired to renewable energy certificates (RECS), supplying Singapore with substantial and sustainable energy from the region.

RECs are instruments which verify generation of renewable energy, with each REC representing the non-power, environmental attributes of 1 MWh of renewable energy generated. Under the Oct 27 revised Singapore Standard 673 Code of Practice for Renewable Energy Certificates, RECs must be linked to renewable electricity physically supplied to Singapore’s local power grid. Previously, due to Singapore’s limited renewable energy resources and imports, entities were allowed to procure RECs that were not tied to electricity delivered to Singapore’s grid.

Certification of the associated environmental attributes of RECs will be facilitated by T-RECs Energy and offered to customers as an option.

Tuas Power COO Michael Wong says that the potential collaboration with EDL and PSTG provides Tuas Power with the option to offer customers with immediate bundled renewable energy solutions. “With a ramp up to 500 MW over three years and a term of up to 15 years, this supports our long-term roadmap for customers’ decarbonisation and sustainable regional energy transition to a net zero carbon future,” he adds.

EDL managing director Souksavart Sosouphanh says that his company “welcomes the opportunity” to explore the collaboration with Tuas Power and PSTG. “Regional power trade in ASEAN has made good progress in recent years, and we believe deeper cooperation among likeminded partners can support a more integrated ASEAN Power Grid.”

See also: Sembcorp Industries grows Singapore power portfolio with new power plant; to explore energy solutions with DayOne

PTSG chairman Phongsavath Senaphuan says: “We look forward to working with Tuas Power, an experienced power player in the Singapore market with a strong track record in generation and retail, to explore how our hydropower portfolio can serve Singapore’s growing demand for clean energy. We recognise that hydropower is a seasonal resource, and we will work towards a supply profile that is transparent and deliverable, should the arrangement proceed.”

title: Oil surges on signs US may resume military strikes against Iran
article:
(Oct 20): Oil surged on signs the US may resume military strikes against Iran, risking fresh turbulence in the region that may hurt energy flows.

Brent climbed towards US$118 a barrel, hitting the highest level since April, while West Texas Intermediate (WTI) was near US$105. A top commander briefed US President Donald Trump on military options on Thursday, the Wall Street Journal reported. The US leader has repeatedly given signals he may restart airstrikes against Tehran after midterm elections next week.

In Iran, one of the country’s top negotiators, Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, suggested that the Islamic Republic’s positions on ending the war would not be compromised. His remarks followed confirmation from Tehran that officials had received a letter sent by US Vice-President JD Vance, which the WSJ reported as a bid to revive the nations’ peace negotiations.

Global benchmark Brent has rallied 14% in October, hitting a six-month high, despite a revival in flows through the Strait of Hormuz, with producers managing to ship cargoes even with elevated risks to shipping. Low inventories and tight supplies of refined products have also supported prices, in part following waves of Ukrainian attacks on Russian processors.

“Even if physical flows recover, traders will find it difficult to keep short positions for long without the US and Iran formally agreeing to a ceasefire,” said Naohiro Niimura, a partner at energy consultancy firm Market Risk Advisory Co, referring to investors holding wagers on lower crude prices.

Regional risks were in focus again as a tanker was struck by an unknown projectile while completing an outbound transit of Hormuz on Thursday, according to UK Maritime Trade Operations. Meanwhile, ExxonMobil Holdings Corp and Chevron Corp cancelled plans to attend the ADIPEC oil conference in Abu Dhabi next month amid heightened security concerns.

See also: Bangladesh in talks to buy more American gas, says US ambassador

Away from the Middle East, Ukraine’s military has paused its strikes against Russian oil refineries following pressure from President Trump, the WSJ reported, citing people with knowledge of the operations. The unofficial move began early last week and is expected to last until after the US midterms, potentially extending further into November, it said.
• Brent for December settlement, which expires Friday, added 2.4% to US$117.61 a barrel at 9.52am in Singapore.



See also: Petrobras pumps at record as Iran war upends oil markets

The midterms — which will be held on Nov 3, halfway through Trump’s second term — determine control of Congress. Ahead of the contests, national polls show that the war in Iran is unpopular, with many voters also unhappy about rising living expenses, including fuel costs. Average diesel prices have risen almost 80% this year, hitting a record in September.

In Israel, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his allies secured 53 seats in the general election held this week, ahead of the main opposition’s bloc of 48 but short of a majority allowing them to rule without further backing. The country joined with the US to start the war against in Iran in late February with the stated aim of dismantling its nuclear programme.

The oil supermajors will wrap up a flood of earnings this week, with results from ExxonMobil and Chevron due later on Friday. Shell plc chief executive officer Wael Sawan said on Thursday that current oil prices no longer looked temporary because global inventories were so depleted.

title: Seatrium secures $200 million contract from SBM Offshore
article:
Mainboard-listed Seatrium has announced it has won a $200 million contract from SBM Offshore for integration works on a floating, production, storage and offloading (FPSO) vessel.

Seatrium’s scope of work comprises the fabrication of key mooring and riser support structures, flare tower and associated topside support structures, vessel modification and drydocking activities, as well as the integration of topside modules. The scope also includes mechanical completion activities, selected pre-commissioning works, and support for commissioning and sea trials.

Marlin Khiew, executive vice president of Seatrium Energy (Projects) says that the contracts award reinforces Seatrium’s “longstanding” partnership with SBM Offshore. “Leveraging the experience and lessons learned from previous projects, together with our engineering expertise and established track record of delivery with certainty, we are proud to support South America's offshore development and its growing role in global energy supply, contributing to greater energy security and long-term economic growth," adds Khiew, who is also Seatrium’s president of LATAM.

Project execution is expected to commence in the fourth quarter of 2026, with completion scheduled for 2029.

Shares in Seatrium are down one cent, or 0.5%, to $1.83 as at around 10.20 am on Oct 30.

title: Bangladesh in talks to buy more American gas, says US ambassador
article:
(Oct 30): Bangladesh is poised to sign deals to buy more US liquefied natural gas (LNG) as the Trump administration pushes to expand energy exports, says the American ambassador to the country.

Several LNG sales proposals are in various stages of the approval process with the Bangladeshi government, and agreements to buy liquefied petroleum gas could follow, said Ambassador Brent Christensen.

“We think there are going to be several more deals signed soon,” he said in an interview in Dhaka. “We want to make sure that our allies and partners have reliable sources of energy.”

Bangladesh is grappling with a fuel shortfall as the Middle East war has choked LNG shipments from Qatar, the country’s main supplier, behind the Strait of Hormuz. The disruption has forced countries across Asia to seek alternatives, and the US — already the world’s largest exporter of natural gas — is positioning itself to replace lost shipments.

The US estimates Bangladesh’s LNG market could be worth about US$10 billion next year, and it could potentially grow to US$30 billion by 2050, Christensen said. The country’s previous government failed to develop enough new domestic gas supply to offset declining output from older fields, forcing the country to become more reliant on expensive overseas LNG.

Washington and Dhaka signed an energy cooperation memorandum in May that created a framework for US companies to participate in government-to-government procurement of LNG and other types of energy. The pact is part of the White House’s broader push to use commercial diplomacy to boost American exports.

See also: Petrobras pumps at record as Iran war upends oil markets

The US-based unit of Centalion Group Ltd — the trading house formerly known as Gunvor — used the framework to cement a deal to sell American LNG to Bangladesh for more than a decade starting this year.

Chevron Corp, the biggest gas producer in the South Asian nation, is looking to expand, Christensen said.

“Continued domestic gas exploration and production can strengthen energy security, support growth and reduce exposure to market volatility,” Shu Xiong, president and managing director of Chevron Bangladesh, said in an emailed response to questions. “Chevron has supported Bangladesh’s energy development for more than three decades and looks forward to helping power its next chapter.”

See also: Oil jumps with Israeli election and Iran attack report in focus

Energy-equipment provider GE Vernova Inc is also keen to do more business in Bangladesh, Christensen said. GE Vernova didn’t respond to a request for comment.

Beyond natural gas, Christensen said that US developers of small modular nuclear reactors are interested in having discussions with Bangladeshi officials about potential projects.

“We are very active in supporting our companies and identifying opportunities for them and helping them resolve longstanding business issues here,” he said. “No other administration has put anywhere close to this priority on commercial diplomacy.”

title: Stock sell-off deepens on tech earnings, bonds rise
article:
(Oct 30): Technology shares led a global stock sell-off as another round of disappointing earnings accelerated a rotation out of the artificial intelligence (AI) trade and drove investors towards haven assets such as Treasuries. Crude oil rallied.

Futures for the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 Index slid 2.3% after earnings from Amazon.com Inc and Intel Corp underwhelmed and raised fresh concerns about spending on the rollout of the AI technology. Bitcoin fell almost 3% to around US$76,600 after Binance, the world’s largest crypto exchange, suspended all deposits and withdrawals as it investigated a suspected hack.

The Kospi Index — a key barometer of the global AI trade — dropped over 5%, set for its biggest one-day drop in two weeks. Chip heavyweights sold off, dragging the broader MSCI Asia Pacific Index down 1.6%. While tech was the biggest loser, five of the gauge’s 11 subgroups advanced as traders continued to rotate out of the hottest trade of the year. Amazon slumped 7.3% in extended trading, while Intel plunged 23%.

“This earnings season has been tough on AI players, with most getting punished against a backdrop of AI-bubble and inflation fears,” said Anna Wu, an investment strategist and founder of Floodlines Research. “The concern isn’t that AI demand has already slowed. It’s that higher funding costs and credit risk could eventually force hyperscalers to slow their build-out.”

As sentiment worsened, traders sought safety in haven assets such as the Swiss franc, the yen and Treasuries. The Swiss and the Japanese currencies were among the biggest gainers against the dollar among Group-of-10 peers, while US government debt rallied across the curve.

After a three-day rally this week, technology stocks lost momentum on Thursday as Samsung’s earnings fell short of investor expectations and Alphabet Inc posted a record drop following its results announcement.

See also: Tech stocks drop as Alphabet, Samsung disappoint

The latest earnings have deepened doubts over the AI trade, raising questions about whether heavy spending can generate returns quickly enough to justify lofty valuations. Even so, the damage has largely been confined to tech, with more than 400 S&P 500 Index members advancing Thursday as investors rotated into more defensive stocks and haven assets.

Chip stocks were among the hardest hit Thursday, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index falling 1.4%. The Nasdaq 100 gauge dropped 1.4% and the S&P 500 Index retreated 0.3%. Microsoft Corp, though, drew blowout demand for its US$25 billion ($32 billion) debt offering.

“The broader message is that investors want more than AI promises,” said Greg Boland, a market strategist at broker Moomoo. “With technology valuations stretched, the market is demanding clearer evidence that heavy investment will deliver profits and cash flow, driving risk-off sentiment across tech stocks and spilling into Asian markets.”

See also: Asian stocks rise, Treasuries steady before Fed decision

Meanwhile, the yen gained 0.2% to 157.45 per dollar ahead of the Bank of Japan’s interest rate decision.

The central bank is widely expected to keep its benchmark interest rate unchanged on Friday while indicating that underlying inflation has finally reached its 2% target.

Elsewhere, oil rose on signs the US may resume military strikes against Iran, risking fresh turbulence in the region that may hurt energy flows. Brent advanced above US$117 a barrel after swinging more than US$3 in the previous session.

US Treasuries extended their gains from Thursday, when they rallied across the curve as a hedge against a potential economic slowdown. Shorter-dated debt led the advance as traders priced in slightly reduced odds of rate increases by the Federal Reserve in the coming months.

The yield on the benchmark 10-year US Treasury fell two basis points to 4.92% in Asian trading.

The bond rally came even as US data pointed to a resilient economy and persistent price pressures. A day after the Fed kept rates steady, figures showed the economy expanded in the third quarter at the fastest pace in a year, while the personal consumption expenditures price index — the Fed’s preferred inflation gauge — rose 0.5% in September, the most in six months.

“It was another strong round of economic data that shows ongoing inflationary pressures and growth split between the AI buildout and consumption,” said Ian Lyngen at BMO Capital Markets.

title: Indonesia rain set to ease toxic haze in Singapore, Malaysia
article:
(Oct 29): Indonesia is set for more consistent rain next month, providing relief from wildfires that have spewed toxic smoke across Singapore and Malaysia, though widespread downpours are still weeks away.

Rainfall has picked up across Indonesia in recent days, helping to replenish soil moisture after months of severe drought triggered by El Niño, according to weather data. While that’s offered some respite, heavier rain isn’t expected until at least early December in regions such as Kalimantan, where blazes have raged and most of the remaining fire hotspots are located.

The choking haze from Indonesia’s worst fire season in years has cloaked local towns and drifted across neighbouring countries for weeks, closing schools, driving demand for air purifiers and straining diplomatic ties. Singapore’s foreign minister visited Jakarta this week to ease widening tensions, with the two countries agreeing to establish a joint taskforce on forest fires.

Indonesia has received less than a quarter of its normal rainfall since June, according to Atmospheric G2, leaving the landscape bone-dry and making fires often linked to slash-and-burn agricultural practices harder to contain. Nearly 13,500 hotspots have been detected nationwide so far this month, the most since 2015, and adding to high counts in September and August, the forestry ministry’s SiPongi platform shows.

“Substantial rainfall should fall through November, generally increasing further in December and remaining significant into early 2027,” said Andreas Vallgren, chief science officer at weather intelligence firm Ignitia. “Whether this is sufficient to extinguish existing fires, particularly in peatlands, will depend on how consistently rainfall reaches the affected areas.”

See also: RegCo issues additional queries to SGX-listed companies with links to haze

Over recent weeks, Kuala Lumpur and Singapore have frequently topped the rankings of the world’s most polluted cities, according to data from IQAir. The city-state has flagged possible legal action against companies suspected of illegal burning, while more than 1,000 people protested in central Jakarta on Wednesday over the government’s handling of the fires.

Indonesia’s agricultural activity has been impacted. Smog from the wildfires is impairing the activity of weevils that pollinate oil palms in the world’s biggest grower, while haze is slowing harvesting at estates owned by major producer SD Guthrie Bhd (KL:SDG) in Kalimantan and Sumatra, and could weigh on productivity.

The combination of fires and dry weather has prompted the Indonesian Palm Oil Association to trim its production estimates for next year to 56.6 million tonnes, a two-year low, according to M Hadi Sugeng Wahyudiono, secretary general of the industry group. That compares with an earlier forecast of 59 million tonnes.

See also: Singapore expands haze inquiries to 10 locally based firms

Still, forecasts point to improving conditions. Near-normal rainfall is expected next month, helping to prevent new fires from developing and curb the spread of existing blazes, according to weather forecasting startup Plannette AI. “Rains will ease fires in Borneo and Sumatra” by December, said chief executive officer and founder Hansi Singh.

Indonesian authorities are hopeful the fire crisis can be resolved in November, said Budi Harsoyo, a senior official at the country’s national weather agency, known as BMKG. Satellite monitoring suggests that the development of hotspots in three provinces hit hardest by fires may be letting up, he added.

There are rising chances of monthly rainfall exceeding 300mm in parts of South Sumatra, Central Kalimantan and South Kalimantan in December, BMKG said this week. Precipitation is expected to pick up in the first week of the month, according to an outlook from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts.

One wildcard risk, said Ignitia’s Vallgren, is that the persistence of fires and smoke can crimp rainfall, because the smog blocks sunrays and inhibits the convective process that forms storms and showers.

History offers a cautionary tale. In 1997, blazes that burned and grew during the prolonged dry season that year were briefly suppressed when rains finally arrived in December, weeks later than normal, but reignited in early 1998 as the rainy season ended prematurely due to a lingering El Niño.

“There is a feedback loop — more fires mean more smoke, which can act to suppress rainfall, which in turn can delay rainfall,” Vallgren said. On the other hand, “if some strong rainfall events make it, they do help to clean the air to some degree, which helps kick-start more frequent storms”.

title: US stock rotation hits AI winners on spending worries
article:
(Oct 30): A selloff in several tech companies spurred a rotation into a broader category of stocks while fueling a push toward the safety of bonds.

The record plunge in Alphabet Inc shares on disappointing sales revived doubts over the artificial-intelligence trade. The Nasdaq 100 lost 1.4%. Microsoft Corp drew blowout demand for its US$25 billion debt offering. In late hours, Amazon.com Inc slumped as its spending soared on efforts to meet demand for AI services. Intel Corp.’s revenue forecast missed estimates.

Not every tech firm fell, but a basket of AI winners sank 2.7%. In a sign of rotation, over 400 shares in the S&P 500 rose.

Thursday’s price action was a “microcosm” of what the stock market has experienced for much of October: Concerns about the AI trade weighing on technology and communication services, but leaving other areas relatively unscathed, said Chris Larkin at E*Trade from Morgan Stanley.

Tech losses revived the haven appeal of Treasuries, with short-dated notes outperforming. Oil wavered as traders parsed conflicting signals on the direction of US military strategy in Iran.

Just a day after the Federal Reserve left rates steady, data showed the US economy expanded in the third quarter at the fastest pace in a year. Meanwhile, the personal consumption expenditures price index — the Fed’s preferred inflation measure — rose 0.5% in September, the most in six months.

See also: Tech stocks slide as Alphabet’s record plunge revives AI fears

“It was another strong round of economic data that shows ongoing inflationary pressures and growth split between the AI buildout and consumption,” said Ian Lyngen at BMO Capital Markets.

AI is still the major theme for activity, but economic resilience is still a broad-based story, according to Eli Nir and Oscar Munoz at TD Securities.

“Couple that with the AI-led inflationary pressures, and it’s clear why the Fed both upgraded its growth assessment and remained acutely focused on their inflation mandate,” they added.

See also: Pimco offloads billions in AI debt just in time to skirt losses — Bloomberg

White House National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett hinted that he expected the Fed would raise rates if inflation figures for this month are elevated.

“If October comes out really high, then I think the Fed would probably appropriately act,” he told Bloomberg Television.

Elsewhere, European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde played down the danger that inflation will spread beyond energy after news that she’ll step down early overshadowed a decision to leave rates untouched.

title: Tech stocks slide as Alphabet’s record plunge revives AI fears
article:
(Oct 30): Tech stocks were dragged lower by a record drop in Alphabet Inc after disappointing results renewed investor concerns about the threat that artificial intelligence (AI) poses to its core business.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 Index was down 1.4% as of 12.15pm in New York, while the S&P 500 fell 0.4%. Stocks outside the tech sector were broadly higher, with around 390 stocks in the benchmark index gaining while the S&P 500 Equal Weight Index advanced 0.9%.

Alphabet shares fell 10%, setting the stock up for its biggest-ever market value wipeout, after the company reported disappointing search and advertising sales that reinforced worries about AI’s threat to its core business.

“After missing forecasts on essentially every key metric except cloud revenue tonight, Google is playing the AI Hunger Games from a position of weakness,” Michael O’Rourke, chief market strategist at JonesTrading Institutional Services LLC, wrote in a note on Wednesday. “Disappointing results in advertising, a business it and Meta Platforms dominate globally, illustrate the key risk investors fear.”

The latest earnings have renewed doubts over the AI trade, raising questions about whether significant spending on the technology can generate returns quickly enough to justify lofty valuations. Investors will get even more earnings to parse when Amazon.com Inc reports after the market closes on Thursday.

Chip stocks took a hit, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index falling 1%. Software shares were also lower on Thursday after disappointing quarterly results from ServiceNow Inc and Fortinet Inc added to the broader concerns. The companies’ shares traded down by 26% and 21%, respectively.

See also: Pimco offloads billions in AI debt just in time to skirt losses — Bloomberg

Investors were slightly more encouraged by Microsoft Corp, which reported earnings after the close on Wednesday. The company posted surging growth in its cloud business while keeping its capital expenditures in check. Shares fell 1.3% on Thursday.

Meanwhile Caterpillar Inc, which builds power-generation equipment used for data centres, saw its shares slump 8.1% after posting third-quarter earnings that only modestly beat expectations.

Outside of AI, DoorDash Inc shares gained 4.5% after the company reported earnings that beat estimates and announced its US$17 billion deal to buy Instacart.

See also: S&P 500 churns in countdown to Fed, tech earnings

Stocks ended the day higher on Wednesday after the Federal Reserve voted to hold interest rates steady.
• Cruise stocks like Royal Caribbean Cruises Ltd and Carnival Corp gained after Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings Ltd raised its full-year guidance in a sign that turnaround efforts are taking hold. The stock jumped 10%.
• Payment stocks are gaining after Mastercard Inc reported better-than-anticipated earnings due to more spending from US consumers.
